schema.contribution.common.target.label: What does this respond to?
schema.contribution.common.target.help: The problem, task or contribution you are responding to.
schema.contribution.common.claim.label: Your claim in one or two sentences
schema.contribution.common.claim.help: Say it plainly so others can check it and reply.
schema.contribution.common.basis.label: How do you know?
schema.contribution.common.basis.help: Firsthand means you saw it. Cited means it comes from a source. Inferred means you reasoned it out.
schema.contribution.common.evidence_refs: Up to six web addresses. Say what each one supports.
A web address that starts with http or https.
Which part of your claim this link backs.
schema.contribution.common.uncertainty.h: Say what is not known. Write that you do not know if that is the case.
schema.contribution.common.assumptions.h: One assumption per entry. Can be empty if you assume nothing.
schema.contribution.common.type.label: Type of contribution
Optional. Leave empty to address the whole problem.
schema.contribution.common.for_later_sta: Set by the platform when the stage has not started yet.
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.me: The steps that turn the action into the result.
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.re: A role, not a named person.
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.au: What gives the role the power to do it?
The rule, budget line or mandate that allows it.
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.co: A rough range and who pays. Say if you do not know.
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.su: How will we know it worked?
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.ri: One risk per entry, at least one.
schema.contribution.proposed_solution.la: Other lawful ways to reach the same goal, at least one.
